caseno: Civil Revision No. 55 of 1984 with Civil Rule No. 39 (R) of 1984.
lawyer:
AKM Shafiqur Rahman with Mostafa Kamal Pasha and Shahabuddin Faiz ----- For the Petitioners. 
SC Das with Rabi Sankar Chakraborty ----- For the Opposite Parties.
parties:
Abdul Hafez and another ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Lal Meah & others ----- Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
This Rule under section 115 (1) of the Civil Procedure Code is directed against the judgment and decree of the learned Sub-ordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Chittagong, passed in Title Appeal No. 166 of 1979 reversing those of the learned Munsif, North Rauzan, Chittagong passed in other Suit No. 250 of 1914.

2. The petitioners as plaintiffs filed the suit against the defendants opposite-parties praying for the following reliefs:— Civil Revision No. 194 of 1983.

(ক) নিম্ন তপসীলের পুকুরের ৮৭৪৬ দাগের RS খতিয়ানের মন্তব্য ঘরের লিখিত ৭/৯ অংশ সংক্রান্ত ১,০৮,৮/১ শতক জমিতে মুল বিবাদীর পূর্ববর্তী ক্রমে কোন স্বত্ব স্বামিত্ব না থাকায় উচ্চারনের ডিক্রি প্রচারিত হয়।

(খ) উক্ত ১/২নং তপসীলের সম্পূর্ণ পুকুরে বাদী ও মোঃ বিবাদী এজমালে দখল থাকার প্রতিকুলে মুল বিবাদী কোন বিঘ্ন না জমাইবার স্বত্ববান নহেন উচ্চারিত হয়।

(গ) বাদী ও মোকাবিলা বিবাদীর স্বত্ব দখলীয় উক্ত পুকুরে মুল বিবাদী অনাধিকার প্রবেশ না করিবার জন্য এবং তৎপ্রতি হস্তক্ষেপ না করার জন্য তদুপরি negative specific relief of permanent injunction জারী হয়।

(ঘ) মোকদ্দমা দায়ের অবস্থায় (গ) প্রার্থনা মতে বাদী ও মোঃ বিবাদীর ১/২ নং তপসীলের পনীর উক্ত জমিতে প্রবেশ না করার ও তাহার প্রতি হস্তক্ষেপ না করার জন্য অস্থায়ী নিষেধাজ্ঞা জারী হয়।

(ঙ) বাদী ও মোঃ বিবাদী অশুদ্ধ RS ৩২৭৪ নং ৩২৮৭ নং খতিয়ান এবং অশুদ্ধ RS খতিয়ান দ্বারা বাধ্য না হওয়া উচ্চারিত হয়।

(চ) মোকদ্দমার খরচ আপত্তিকারী বিবাদীর বিরুদ্ধে ডিক্রি হয়।

3. The plaintiff's case in short is that the disputed tank belonged to Bakar Ali, Gul Banu and Bhagyabati Gul Banu and Bhagyabati had no heir except Bakar Ali. Bakar Ali was great grandfather of plaintiff No. 1. Maghi survey was made in the names of Bakar Ali, Gul Banu and Bhagyabati. CS Khatian stands recorded in the name of Uzir Ali who was son of Baker Ali. MS plot No. 6998 corresponding to CS plot No. 7190 was in possession of Md Waresh Ali who was in Chasha (cultivator) under plaintiffs predecessors. RS Khatian was wrongly prepared in respect of the disputed tank and it was recorded as RS plot 8746. Recording of 7/9th share in the names of defendants predecessors was wrong. Uzir Ali died leaving sons Asmat Ali, Ismat Ali and Hamdu Meah. The plaintiff No. 2 and proforma defendant 43 are the heirs of Hamdu Meah. lsmat Ali died leaving sons, plaintiff No. 1 and proforma defendant No. 42. The plaintiffs are possessing the disputed tank for generations. PS and BS khatian also are wrongly recorded. The plaintiffs transferred 2 gondas of land to Gura Meah and 2 gondas of land to Yakub Ali. The defendants have no share in the disputed tank.

4. The defendants 2 and 8 contested the suit by filing joint written statement contending, inter-alia, that the suit is not maintainable and it barred by limitation. The defendants are the heirs of Gut Banu and Bhagyabati. Gul Banu and Bhagyabati were not related to Baker Ali Md Zaman was the husband of Gul Banu and Hari Chand was the husband of Bhagyabati. Gul Banu died leaving son Abdul. Abdul died leaving two sons namely, Mohsen Ali and Malekazzaman. Mohsen Ali died leaving two sons namely, Torab Ali and Amjad Ali. Torab Ali died leaving three sons namely, Chunnu Meah, Sultan Ahmed and Lal Meah. Sultan Ahmed died leaving widow Abeda Khatun and daughter defendant No. 1 Gul Safa Khatun. Lal Mueah died leaving widow Sanwara Begum and brother Chunnu Meah. Chunnu Meah transferred his share to defendant No. 2 Lal Meah Amjad Ali died leaving three namely, Chunnu Meah Yakub Ali and Akmal Ali. The defendants Nos. 6 to 11 are the heirs of Yakub Ali, Abdul Sobhan purchased the share of Malekazzaman for his heirs. Bhagyabati died leaving Md. Waresh Md. Waresh died leaving Mubarak Ali Mubarak Ali died leaving daughter Amirun Nessa who sold her share to Abdul Malek. CS. Khatian was recorded in the names of predecessors of the plaintiffs, and the defendants. RS. Khatian was recorded correctly. PS. Khatian and BS Khatian are prepared in the names of defendants. The principal defendants (1-10) are in possession of 7/9the share of the disputed tank. The principal defendants have graveyard on the eastern and western banks of the disputed tank. The principal defendants have cowshed and haystack on the western bank of the disputed tank. They have 4 outer houses on the western bank of the disputed tank. The Plaintiffs and proforma defendants (41-56) got 2/9th share of the disputed tank.

5. The learned Munsif found that the plaintiffs having paid the advalorem court fees as per Courts Direction in the plaintiff’s prayer "for declaration that the recording of 7/9th share in the disputed tank in RS. Plot No. 8746 is wrong and also for declaration that in spite of that wrong recording the plaintiff's right and interest has not been affected" the suit for declaration of title and confirmation of possession and, as such, the suit as framed was maintainable. The learned Munsif further found that Maghi Chitta is a document of title, that Gul Banu and Bhagyabati were the predecessors of the plaintiffs 41-56, that the defendants suggestion that Md. Waresh Ali, the predecessor of defendants 23-29, 33-35 and 37-40, was the son of Bhagyabati was disproved by CS Khatian Exhibit 1(f) and a and that the descendants of Chasa Md. Waresh Ali got their names recorded with their masters' descendants. He also found that the recording of the 7/9th share in the names of the defendants' predecessors during the RS. Operation was wrong and the plaintiffs are entitled to get a declaration to that effect and that the suit having been filed within 6 years from 15-5-74 on which date defendants threatened the plaintiffs with dispossession on the basis of wrong entry in the RS Khatian, the suit was not barred by limitation or adverse possession. Accordingly the learned Munsif decreed the suit in part declaring that the recording of RS Khatian, Exhibit A (1) and A (2) to the extent of 7/9th share in the names of the defendants' predecessors was wrong and that the right of the plaintiffs and proforma defendants Nos. 41 to 56 to the extent of 16 annas share in the disputed tank has not been affected by RS. Khatians in dispute and further declaring that the plaintiffs and the proforma defendants joint possession with defendants who had purchased 4 gandas of land out of the disputed tank appertaining to RS Plot No. 8746 from the plaintiff No 1 be confirmed. Against the judgment and decree of the learned Munsif the contesting defendants 2 and 8 prepared the appeal and the plaintiffs-respondents in the appeal filed cross-objection for cost of suit. On consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence on record, the learned Sub-ordinate Judge found that in the plaint there is no clear mention of declaration of title in the disputed property, that two negative prayers in prayer (kha) make it affirmative i.e. it tantamount to the position that the principal defendants have got right to disturb in the possession of the entire disputed tank of schedules 1-2 of the plaint, that from the prayer portion of the plaint it appears that schedule 1 property is disputed i.e. 7/9 th share and schedule 2 i.e. 2/9th share is not disputed and thus it creates contradiction in the prayer (kha) and that the negative specific relief of permanent injunction in prayer (ga) is a vague term. The learned Sub-ordinate Judge further found that the recording of RS Khatian in the names of principal defendants is correct, that the principal defendants have possession in the disputed tank, that the Maghi Chitta cannot alone create title in favour or the plaintiffs for the disputed tank and that the plaintiffs side having not rectified the recording of the RS Khatian by filing any suit/case the question of limitation for challenging the RS Khatian also arises, that the plaintiffs and the proforma defendants have joint possession in the disputed tank along with the principal defendants, that the RS Khatian cannot be rectified as the plaintiffs did not take to correct it within the period of limitation, that in the absence of direct evidence the presumption of RS Khatian cannot be rebutted that there is no clear claim by the plaintiff's side that they have title in the entire disputed tank, that the suit is not maintainable and it is barred by limitation. Accordingly he allowed the appeal and rejected the cross-objection and dismissed the suit in reversal of the judgment and decree of the learned Munsif. Against the judgment and decree of the learned Sub-ordinate Judge the plaintiffs have obtained the present Rule.

6. Mr AKM Shafiqur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiffs-petitioners, has contended that the trial Court having directed the plaintiffs to pay advalorem Court fee and the plaintiffs having done so, the suit as framed is maintainable and the finding of the trial Court as to the maintainability of the suit having not been adverted to or reversed by the learned Subordinate Judge the decision of the learned Sub-ordinate Judge that the suit is not maintainable is not sustainable in law. In sup-port of his contention he has relied upon the case of Pakistan vs Muhammad Abdul Kuddus, Income Tax Officer, (1968) 20 DLR 332 and the case of Mst. Rabeya Khatun vs Md. Elias Molla and others, (1976) 28 DLR (HC) 181. In the case reported in 20 DLR 332 the plaintiff prayed for declaration that the order posting his as Income Tax officer be declared illegal and inoperative and it was held in that case that the plaintiff was entitled to a declaration that his appointment as Income Tax Officer. Class 11, Grade 111 was illegal, void and inoperative although the declaration sought for was couched in a negative form, namely that order posting him as Income Tax Officer be declared illegal and inoperative. In the present case as correctly noted by the learned Sub-ordinate judge the plaintiffs did not pray for declaration of title and confirmation of possession and made two negative and contradictory prayers in prayer (kha)of the plaint and a prayer for a negative specific relief of permanent injunction in a vague term in prayer (ga) of the plaint. Thus the facts of the case reported in 20 DLR 332 are distinguishable from those of the present case and, as such, the proposition of law enunciated in 20 DLR 332 is not applicable in the present case. In the case reported in 28 DLR 181 upon the facts that the plaintiff prayed for a decree that a sale deed executed by the defendants 1-2 in favour of defendant No. 3 relating to self-same property was void, illegal, inoperative, collusive and the defendants 1-2 acquired no interest in the said property and hence not binding on the plaintiff, it was held: "the prayer in the plaint, though not drafted happily, leaves no doubt that what the plaintiff was essentially seeking in the suit was a declaration that their right, title and interest have not been affected by transaction of sale in favour of the defendants Nos. 1 and 2 or in favour of defendants No. 3. We cannot therefore, say that the suit as framed does not fall within the purview of section 42 of the Specific Relief act and that should be thrown out as not maintainable." In the case of Mst Rabeya Khatun vs Md. Eleas Molla and others 28 DLR 181 the prayer in the plaint left no doubt that what the plaintiff was essentially seeking in the suit was for declaration that their right, title and interest were not affected by the transaction of sale but in the present case the plaintiffs have not at all prayed for declaration of title and confirmation of possession and have made negative contradictory and vague prayers. Thus the facts of 28 DLR 181 are different from the facts of the present case and, as such, the principal laid down in the case reported in 28 DLR 181 has no application in the present case.

7. Mr. SC Das, the learned Advocate appearing for the OPs 1 and 2, has contended that the learned Munsif has erred in proceeding to dispose of the case from a wrong premise namely, that the suit is one for declaration of title and confirmation of possession though from the pleadings and the reliefs prayed for it is nowhere found that it is a suit for declaration of title and confirmation of possession as the plaintiffs have not prayed for declaration of title and confirmation of possession.

8. It is found that the learned Sub-ordinate Judge has reversed the finding of learned Munsif that the suit was one for declaration of title and confirmation of possession inasmuch as, the plaintiffs in their pleading relief prayed for did not pray for declaration of title and confirmation of possession and has found that the suit is not maintainable. It cannot be said that merely because the plaintiffs paid the advalorem court fees as per direction of the Court, the suit in effect became a suit for declaration of title and confirmation of possession and, as such, maintainable in the absence of prayer for declaration of title and confirmation of possession in the pleading or in the reliefs prayed for. The finding of the learned Sub-ordinate Judge that the suit is not maintainable in due to the negative, contradictory and vague prayers of the plaintiffs in the reliefs prayed for in the plaint. For the above reasons, I am of the opinion that the learned Sub-ordinate Judge has correctly found that the suit as framed is not maintainable in as, much as, no relief can be given to the plaintiffs as per their negative, contradictory and vague prayer in the plaint.

9. On the point of limitation the learned advocate for the petitioner has contended that the suit having been instituted within 6 years from the date of threatened dispossession on 15-5-74, the suit is in time. In support of his contention he has relied upon the case of Rai Kiran Chandra Ray Bahadur vs Tarak Nath Gongopadhy, 40 CWN 566 which were relied upon by the learned Munsif. In the case reported in 40 CWN 566 it was held: If there is an entry adverse to the plaintiff he is not bound to institute suit for declaration that the entry is wrong. He can wait and when an invasion on his right is made on the basis of the entry, he can come and sue for a declaration of his title on the ground that the record is wrong. Such a suit will be in time if brought within 6 years of the threatened invasion.

10. Mr SC Das, the learned Advocate for the opposite-parties 1 and 2 has further contended that the RS record showing that the predecessors of principal defendants and proforma defendants have been in possession of 7/9th share of the suit tank and the suit having not been instituted within 12 years it is barred by limitation and in the absence prayer for consequential relief by way of recovery of possession the suit is not maintainable. The learned Sub-ordinate Judge having found that the plaintiffs and proforma defendants are in joint possession of the disputed tank, along with the principal defendants and thus the principal defendants having become co-sharers of the plaintiffs and proforma defendants, I think the question of adverse possession and the prayer for consequential relief by way of possession does not arise in the present case and plaintiffs having instituted that suit within six years from the date of threatened dispossession on 15-5-74 as per finding of the learned Munsif which is neither adverted to nor reversed by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge I opine in the light of the case reported in 40 C W N 566 that the suit is within time under Article 120 of the Limitation Act.

<u>11. In support of the finding of the Sub-ordinate Judge that the Maghi chitta does not create title, Mr. SC Das, the learned Advocate for the opposite-parties 1-2 refers the case of Fazlur Rahim vs Nabendra Krishna Roy and others 17 CWN 151 and the case of Prodyot Kumar Sen Gupta vs Nagendra Kumar Chowdhury, 52 CWN 72. In 17 CWN 151 it was held that a chitta prepared by the Government when interested as a proprietor of the estate concerned could not be said to be a public document and that no special presumption attached to these chittas. In 52 CWN 72 it was held:-It is not necessary for us to hold that Maghi Chitta is wrong. Each record must be presumed to be correct at its date, and since the position indicated by the entries in the chittas could, during the interval, well change into the position indicated by the cadastral and revisional survey records, the latter position is not shown to be impossible or invalid in law, as the learned Sub-ordinate Judge erroneously supposed." In the light of the above cases reported in 17 CWN 151 and 52 CWN 72 it can safely be held that Maghi chitta did not create title in favour of the plaintiff in the disputed tank as has been correctly found by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge and the latter position indicated by the RS record is valid in law. As to the presumption of RS khatian and its rebuttal the learned Advocate for the opposite-parties 1-2, has referred to the case of Akrab Ali vs Zahiruddin Kari, 30 DLR (AD) 81 and the case of Meherjan Bibi vs Naimuddin Dhali being dead Raisuddin and others 33 DLR 127 in the case reported in 30 DLR (AD) 81 it is held that according to section 103B(5) of the Bengal Tenancy Act every entry in a record of right finally published shall be evidence of the matter referred to in such entry and shall be presumed to be correct until it is proved to be incorrect. In 33 DLR 126 it is held that the presumption of correction as available on the strength of section 103 B (5) of the Bengal Tenancy Act, has got to be rebutted by the person who alleges it. In the light of the proposition of law enunciated in the Appellate Division case reported in 30 DLR (AD) 81 the RS Khatian in the present case raises a presumption of its correctness until proved to be incorrect and in view of the decisions in 33 DLR 126 the onus is on the plaintiffs to rebut the presumption of the correctness of the RS khatian in the present case in as, much as, the plaintiffs have alleged that the entry of the RS khatian is wrong. The learned Sub-ordinate Judge has correctly found that there is no direct evidence in the case to rebut presumption of the RS khatian. As such the correctness of the entry of the RS Khatian is not rebutted in the present case.</u>

For the reasons stated above, I am of the opinion that the learned Sub-ordinate Judge has correctly held that the suit is not maintainable, that the Maghi chitta created no title in favour of plaintiffs and the RS recording is correct but he is not correct in holding that the suit is barred by limitation.

In the result, the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs. The connected Civil Rule No. 39 (R) of 1984 is discharged.

End.
